Definition: to lie (i.e. deceive), literally or figuratively
BiblicalUsage: Kazab means to lie, to deceive, to tell a lie: 2 Kings 4:16 has the Shunammite begging Elisha, do not lie unto thine handmaid, when he promises her a son. Job 24:25 challenges, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth? Psalms 116:11 says, I said in my haste, all men are liars. Micah 2:11 warns of a man walking in falsehood who says, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lie wears many coats: a prophet's promise of wine, a hasty word about all men, a fear that God's promise is too good. I hold that God calls the liar what he is, and his own promises are the one place a lie cannot live.
